title: introduce-token-runway-heatmap-aggregator-and-pacing-controller
author: Aisha Rahman
release_notes: Adds a new offline heatmap aggregator and pacing controller for token runway simulation workloads. No API changes to public runner interfaces. Includes new telemetry exports and a dashboard snapshot template.
description:
Motivation: We need a lightweight, reproducible way to surface per-token heat and runway (tokens remaining before KVC cache eviction) across representative session workloads for long-context models. This PR introduces two coordinated components: (1) token_runway_heatmap_aggregator (offline reporter) which aggregates token runway histograms and produces heatmap tiles and (2) pacing_controller which feeds the runner with controlled inter-request pacing policies to exercise tail/backpressure behavior.

What this does: Adds a workload that simulates mixed-length sessions with variable primer lengths and produces a tiled heatmap export that correlates token position, KV cache eviction distance, and latency p95. The pacing controller implements: fixed-pace, poissonized-pace, and burst-window pacing strategies with tunable burst size and cooldown. The aggregator produces both compact tile protobufs (for fast downstream ingestion) and CSV fallbacks for ad-hoc analysis.

Compatibility & safety: No changes to public APIs consumed by other benchmark suites. New components live under benchmark-lab/token_runway and are opt-in from the CLI via --workload token-runway-heatmap. Default runs keep disk footprint < 200MB for 1M tokens sampled.

Telemetry & dashboards: The aggregator emits telemetry to /telemetry/heatmaps as gzipped protobuf blobs and emits metadata metrics for p50/p90/p95/p99 latency correlated by token-offset buckets. Included in this PR is a Grafana dashboard JSON snapshot (token-runway-heatmap-snapshot.json) to visualize runway vs latency heatmap.

Performance results (local cluster): On a 4xA10p cluster we observed stable runway heat islands where p95 increases ~1.6x at runway < 64 tokens; the pacing controller allows reproducing microburst amplification factors up to 2.8x depending on batch coalescing settings. Example test run saved in artifacts/2026-02-20-run-03.tar.gz.

Files changed: See changed_files field for highlights.

Testing: Unit tests cover pacing policy transitions and tile serialization. Integration smoke runs against the micro-cluster harness were added to CI. Benchmarks include deterministic seed to ensure repeatability.

Rollout plan: Feature flagged behind BENCH_TOKEN_RUNWAY. Merge to main, then add to nightly matrix for two weeks, collect drift alerts; if stable, promote to weekly open benchmarks.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of aggregator + controller
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration smoke runs in CI
- [x] Dashboard snapshot and run artifact attached
- [x] Linear tickets linked

Related: ENG-2149 (runway observability), ENG-2201 (pacing and backpressure experiments).
